title: carex maritima subsp. lyngbyei
intro: Carex maritima subsp. lyngbyei, commonly known as Lyngbye's sedge, is a subspecies of sedge that belongs to the family Cyperaceae. It is a flowering plant native to the coastal regions of Iceland, Greenland, and the Faroe Islands. The plant has been traditionally used in folk medicine, and its health benefits include its anti-inflammatory and antibacterial properties, which can aid in wound healing and alleviate respiratory issues. The bioactive constituents of Carex maritima subsp. lyngbyei include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and glycosides, which contribute to its therapeutic actions such as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial activities.
